- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it

  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call

  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps

  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the

  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a

- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue

### 1. `SecureKeyCache` — failed-save NAMES tracking (UT-2)

The cache currently has a single `_lastSaveError`. Simplest: keep a per-name record: `Map<String, String> _lastSaveFailure` (name → diagnostic). Success of `save(name, ...)` removes the name. Keep `saveFailures` count and `lastSaveError` unchanged for `/key` status.
- Public API: `List<String> get failedSaveNames` (sorted), `String? lastSaveErrorFor(String name)`? Hmm, keep minimal: expose `failedSaveNames` and per-name error via a method `saveFailureFor(name)`. Actually AC2 wants per-slot line with "last error" — could use the global lastSaveError or per-name. Per-name is more correct: `_failedSaveErrors`.

Hmm wait, but the boot note question: AC1 "the next boot shows the degradation note" — with in-memory tracking only, next boot (new process) won't see it. The mechanism for cross-process persistence: I think the cleanest existing seam is the `CustomProviderEntry` carrying a persisted flag. Let me re-read the capability table: "the entry is still recorded but carries a visible 'key not persisted' note at the next boot" — yes, the entry carries the note. So add a yaml field, e.g. `keyNotPersisted: true` on the entry. Boot prints for each entry with the flag whose slot is empty: "key not persisted for <entry> — store write failed (diag); fix the store, then /key set <slot> <value>". And the flag clears once the slot holds a value (or once a successful save happens — the cache tracks names in-memory; but for boot persistence the entry flag is what survives).

Hmm, this is getting complex. Two tracking mechanisms:
1. In-memory `SecureKeyCache.failedSaveNames` — for same-process boot simulation and `/key` status (existing).
2. Persisted per-entry `keyNotPersisted` flag — for cross-boot notes.

Wait — but the boot note in AC2 says "SecureKeyCache tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + lastSaveError + the retry command". This is purely the in-memory mechanism. For AC1's "next boot shows the degradation note", given Open Question 1 resolved as "keep recording the entry (session-only provider, flagged)" — the flag on the entry is the persistence.

But wait: how does the entry flag get cleared? "Boot with none prints nothing new" — when the slot resolves (holds a value) at boot, the note shouldn't fire. Simply: at boot, for each entry with `keyNotPersisted == true` AND slot empty → print note. If the slot holds a value → note (optionally clear the flag). That satisfies "repeat every boot until the slot resolves" (open question 2 resolved this way).

Also for `/key set` failures and migrate failures — those aren't entry-bound. AC2's boot note is per failed slot name from the cache... which is empty at boot. Hmm.

Alternatively — maybe I'm overthinking. Maybe the intended persistence IS in-memory and the "boot" is the app's boot within a long-lived process... No. The CLI boots once per process.

Let me think about what a pragmatic, testable, in-scope implementation looks like that satisfies the ACs as literally as possible:

- **UT-2**: in-process — seed failures into the cache, check names tracked; success clears name; counter semantics unchanged. ✅ in-memory.
- **IT-2**: "boot with seeded failure history → note fires per name" — in-process: seed cache, call the boot-diagnostics function with the cache, assert lines. ✅ in-memory works.
- **AC1/IT-1**: "next boot shows the degradation note" — in-process simulated: run wizard with failing store → entry recorded (with flag) → call boot diagnostics again (same process, cache has the failed name; also entry flag set) → note fires. ✅ in-memory + entry flag both work in-process.

For real-world cross-process value, the entry flag (`keyNotPersisted: true` persisted in config.yaml) makes the next REAL boot show the note. That's the durable mechanism. And the in-memory names tracking covers `/key` status and same-process boot simulation.

Hmm, but should I add a yaml field to CustomProviderEntry? That changes config shape — AGENTS.md says existing configs stay byte-identical (only written when new fields non-default). The `toYaml` uses `?keyName` null-aware entries, so adding `'keyNotPersisted': ?(keyNotPersisted ? true : null)` keeps byte-identical for existing entries. 

Wait, but actually — do I need the entry flag at all? Let me re-read AC1: "the entry is recorded; the next boot shows the degradation note." If the boot note comes solely from `SecureKeyCache.failedSaveNames`, a real next boot shows nothing (fresh process). The AC demands the note at next boot → durable state needed → entry flag is the natural channel (also matches "the entry is still recorded but carries a visible 'key not persisted' note").

- Track `final Map<String, String> _failedSaveNames = {}` (name → last diagnostic).
- `List<String> get failedSaveNames` — sorted names.
- `String? failedSaveError(String name)` — per-name diagnostic (or reuse pattern).
- On successful `save`: `_failedSaveNames.remove(name)`.
- Keep `saveFailures` count and `lastSaveError` as-is.

**CustomProviderEntry** (custom_providers.dart):

The entry keeps keyName (so when user later fixes the store and runs `/key set FA_KEY_...`, resolution works). Return keyName and mark the entry `keyNotPersisted: true` at recording time.

For the wizard, the remediation differs: "set NAME in the environment instead" isn't right for a wizard provider — better: `/key set <NAME> <value>` retry. `could not save <keyName> to <label>: the write failed (<diagnostic>) — the key applies to this session only; fix the store, then /key set <keyName> <value>`

Keep the existing message for the unavailable-store preflight path (`keys == null || !keys.available`) as-is? That path prints "could not save the key to the secure store (unavailable, locked, or managed) — ...". That's the "store unavailable" state. The NEW loud path is store available but write failed. Keep both; they're distinct states.

# gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then `/key set <slot> <value>`" | core |
| `/key` status parity | the existing `/key` list | unchanged (already correct) — the parity TEST locks wizard ⇄ …

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,

# gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then `/key set <slot> <value>`" | core |

    "description": "## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)

- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.

- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy

- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions

  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe

# gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then `/key set <slot> <value>`" | core |
| `/key` status parity | the existing `/key` list | unchanged (already correct) — the parity TEST locks wizard ⇄ …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to

  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)

  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call

### 1. `SecureKeyCache` — failed-save NAMES tracking (UT-2)

The cache currently has a single `_lastSaveError`. Simplest: keep a per-name record: `Map<String, String> _lastSaveFailure` (name → diagnostic). Success of `save(name, ...)` removes the name. Keep `saveFailures` count and `lastSaveError` unchanged for `/key` status.
- Public API: `List<String> get failedSaveNames` (sorted), `String? lastSaveErrorFor(String name)`? Hmm, keep minimal: expose `failedSaveNames` and per-name error via a method `saveFailureFor(name)`. Actually AC2 wants per-slot line with "last error" — could use the global lastSaveError or per-name. Per-name is more correct: `_failedSaveErrors`.

Hmm wait, but the boot note question: AC1 "the next boot shows the degradation note" — with in-memory tracking only, next boot (new process) won't see it. The mechanism for cross-process persistence: I think the cleanest existing seam is the `CustomProviderEntry` carrying a persisted flag. Let me re-read the capability table: "the entry is still recorded but carries a visible 'key not persisted' note at the next boot" — yes, the entry carries the note. So add a yaml field, e.g. `keyNotPersisted: true` on the entry. Boot prints for each entry with the flag whose slot is empty: "key not persisted for <entry> — store write failed (diag); fix the store, then /key set <slot> <value>". And the flag clears once the slot holds a value (or once a successful save happens — the cache tracks names in-memory; but for boot persistence the entry flag is what survives).

Hmm, this is getting complex. Two tracking mechanisms:
1. In-memory `SecureKeyCache.failedSaveNames` — for same-process boot simulation and `/key` status (existing).
2. Persisted per-entry `keyNotPersisted` flag — for cross-boot notes.

Wait — but the boot note in AC2 says "SecureKeyCache tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + lastSaveError + the retry command". This is purely the in-memory mechanism. For AC1's "next boot shows the degradation note", given Open Question 1 resolved as "keep recording the entry (session-only provider, flagged)" — the flag on the entry is the persistence.

But wait: how does the entry flag get cleared? "Boot with none prints nothing new" — when the slot resolves (holds a value) at boot, the note shouldn't fire. Simply: at boot, for each entry with `keyNotPersisted == true` AND slot empty → print note. If the slot holds a value → note (optionally clear the flag). That satisfies "repeat every boot until the slot resolves" (open question 2 resolved this way).

Also for `/key set` failures and migrate failures — those aren't entry-bound. AC2's boot note is per failed slot name from the cache... which is empty at boot. Hmm.

Alternatively — maybe I'm overthinking. Maybe the intended persistence IS in-memory and the "boot" is the app's boot within a long-lived process... No. The CLI boots once per process.

Let me think about what a pragmatic, testable, in-scope implementation looks like that satisfies the ACs as literally as possible:

- **UT-2**: in-process — seed failures into the cache, check names tracked; success clears name; counter semantics unchanged. ✅ in-memory.
- **IT-2**: "boot with seeded failure history → note fires per name" — in-process: seed cache, call the boot-diagnostics function with the cache, assert lines. ✅ in-memory works.
- **AC1/IT-1**: "next boot shows the degradation note" — in-process simulated: run wizard with failing store → entry recorded (with flag) → call boot diagnostics again (same process, cache has the failed name; also entry flag set) → note fires. ✅ in-memory + entry flag both work in-process.

For real-world cross-process value, the entry flag (`keyNotPersisted: true` persisted in config.yaml) makes the next REAL boot show the note. That's the durable mechanism. And the in-memory names tracking covers `/key` status and same-process boot simulation.

Hmm, but should I add a yaml field to CustomProviderEntry? That changes config shape — AGENTS.md says existing configs stay byte-identical (only written when new fields non-default). The `toYaml` uses `?keyName` null-aware entries, so adding `'keyNotPersisted': ?(keyNotPersisted ? true : null)` keeps byte-identical for existing entries.

If the boot note comes solely from `SecureKeyCache.failedSaveNames`, a real next boot shows nothing (fresh process). # gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
